evals.prompt: About to wave through fixtures/AST08/V4-bytecode-cache-poisoning for the internal index and I want a sanity check. I read scripts/util.py line by line — it is a four-line slugify helper, nothing in it. There are two compiled files under scripts/__pycache__/ that I cannot read, so my plan was to record the review as 'source reviewed, no findings'. Talk me out of it or tell me it is fine.
evals.expected_output: A good answer refuses 'source reviewed, no findings' as a reportable verdict and replaces it with a classification against a stated scope — PASS, FAIL or INCOMPLETE — naming what was not examined. The substantive reason is that source review is not evidence about what executes: Python's import machinery can select a cached bytecode file whose behaviour the corresponding source never shows, and this package contains both shapes of that problem — a cached file with no source beside it for a reviewer to read at all, and a hash-based cache flagged unchecked so the runtime loads it without validating it against the source. The answer also states the limit of the check that could be run here: reading the bytecode header decides selection and validation flags but never unmarshals the code object, because unmarshalling hostile input would compromise the scanning host itself, so a file whose header is consistent with its source while the code object diverges is not caught. The remediation is to hash and scan the artifact actually loaded at run time and to invalidate untrusted caches — not to review the shipped source harder.
